q: Do I need an account to use Fridge Pick?
a: No. There is no sign-up or sign-in. Open the app and start using it right away.
Yes. All dishes, recipes and photos are built into the app, and it never connects to the internet. You only need a connection to install or update it from the App Store or Google Play.

q: Why don’t I see some dishes in the Cookbook?
a: A dish is left off the Cookbook when you hid it, when it contains one of your allergens (with Hide dishes with my allergens on), when it needs an ingredient you excluded, or when a filter is on. Seasonal keeps only dishes tagged for the current season, so all-year dishes stay off that chip. Tap Clear filters if nothing matches, and check the tabs in Settings → Menu to see every dish and why it isn’t shown. Home uses the same allergy, exclusion and kitchen rules, and it also skips dishes you cooked today or yesterday.

q: How do I get a hidden dish back?
a: Open Settings → Menu, go to the Hidden tab and tap Unhide next to the dish. Right after hiding a dish you can also tap Undo.
The Quick filter shows dishes that take about 5 minutes or less. All built-in dishes take 15 minutes or less.

q: What do the badges on a dish mean?
a: A dish you cooked in the last 14 days, including day 14, shows Cooked today, Cooked yesterday or Cooked N days ago. A dish you have never cooked, or last cooked longer ago than that, has no badge. Tap I made this on a dish page to update it.

q: How do I switch between metric and imperial?
a: Open Settings and choose Units: Auto, Metric or Imperial. Auto follows the phone’s measurement settings, or the region when the phone does not report them. The United States, Liberia and Myanmar use imperial in that fallback; every other region uses metric. A UK measurement setting uses imperial (ounces, cups and °F). Nutrition stays in grams.

q: What happened to the Fruits item in My fridge?
a: Fresh fruit is now its own Fruits section, with a chip for each fruit. There is no generic Fruits item. If you had Fruits ticked, the next launch ticks Apple, Banana, Orange, Berries, Grapes, Melon and Watermelon instead, and removes only that old tick. A dish such as fruit salad or yoghurt with fruit accepts any suitable fruit you have. The dish page shows that line as Any fruit.

On Home, the line under the hero reads In season when the season is why that dish is ahead of the next one. The Seasonal filter on the Cookbook keeps dishes tagged for the current season. The hemisphere comes from the phone’s region. A dish is not hidden on Home just for being out of season.

q: Why don’t the recipes use a microwave?
a: The microwave is switched off in Settings → Kitchen by default, so recipes use your stove, steam cooker, oven, toaster or blender instead. You can switch it on, but Fridge Pick still prefers other methods when you have the right appliance.

q: How accurate are the calories and nutrition values?
a: They are approximate values per serving for a typical version of each recipe: calories, protein, carbs and fat. Your portion and products may differ.

q: Can I rely on the allergen labels?
a: Please don’t rely on them alone. Allergen markers are a convenience based on typical recipes and may be incomplete. Ingredients and brands vary, so always check the product labels. The app is not medical advice.

q: Can I use my data on another phone?
a: There are no accounts and no sync, so your fridge, plan, lists and settings stay on the device where you entered them. Your phone’s own backup (iCloud or Google) may include app data, depending on your system settings.

q: How do I delete my data?
a: You can clear parts of it in the app: Clear all in My fridge, Clear week in the week plan, Reset in the shopping list. To delete everything at once, uninstall the app. On Android you can also use Settings → Apps → Fridge Pick → Storage → Clear storage.

q: Where do the dish photos come from?
a: Most are from Wikimedia Commons under Creative Commons licenses, the rest from Unsplash. Authors and licenses are listed on the Photo Credits page.
